reuse.why: The API and forecast reuse getScheduledAmount and approximate amounts reuse getApproxNumberThreshold, but budget templates bypass the complete amount helper.

duplication.why: Budget templates duplicate the operator dispatch already encapsulated by getScheduledAmount, although the underlying arithmetic is shared.

placement.why: Amount policy resides in shared schedule utilities, tolerance remains in shared rules, and API output enrichment stays in the API model.

scope.why: All edits concern schedule amount expectations, their API representation, or accompanying tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared arithmetic is straightforward, but optional operator propagation leaves existing planning consumers outside the approximate policy, while duplicated dispatch and obsolete descriptions increase maintenance effort.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/schedule-template.ts dispatches between range, approximate, and single amounts instead of calling getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: The nested operator ternary in schedule-template.ts reshapes the amount classification already performed by getScheduledAmount rather than delegating that decision.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter and an isapprox branch; schedule-template.ts independently dispatches to its lower-level helpers, and existing preview and balance callers omit the newly required policy context.
